title: What to watch at the open
text: The numbers below are Thursday's closing prices. Tech stocks fell hard that day (the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ lost 2.9%), so at the open the thing to watch is whether chip and AI stocks steady themselves or keep sliding. Calmer holdings like the dividend fund SCHD and Eli Lilly closed near their 52 week highs.

title: Chip stocks are far below their highs
text: Vertiv closed 48.5% below its 52 week high, Broadcom 34.7% below and AMD 22.9% below. A stock that sits far under its high has already had a big fall, which tells you it can swing a lot in both directions. That swing is what the risk score measures.

title: Meta: big drop, analysts still higher
text: Meta closed at $648.85 after a 7.0% drop. The average analyst price target is $834.36, about 28.6% above the price. A price target is only an opinion about where a stock might go in a year, and analysts are often wrong, so treat it as one clue and not a promise.

title: Two stocks closed near the top of their range
text: SCHD closed at $35.40 and Eli Lilly at $1,306.69, both within about 1% of their 52 week highs. Being near a high is not good or bad by itself. It only says the price has already risen a lot, so a small slip is easier to notice.

title: Lesson 20: What is a time horizon?
text: A time horizon is how long you plan to keep your money invested before you need it. Money for a bike next summer has a short horizon. Money for college in 10 years has a long one. This matters because stocks can fall a lot in a few weeks, like they did on Thursday, but over many years they have usually had time to recover. A short horizon means you cannot wait out a drop, so people usually keep that money in safer places like savings or bonds. A long horizon can handle more ups and downs. Before you look at any stock, ask yourself when you will need the money. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
